slides.heading: Colliding Asteroids
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Medium · Stacks
slides.narration: Let's solve Colliding Asteroids, a medium stacks problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: Sign is direction (+ right, - left), magnitude is size.
When they meet the smaller explodes (both if equal).
slides.narration: Here's the problem. Sign is direction ( plus right, - left), magnitude is size. When they meet the smaller explodes (both if equal). Return survivors.

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: Simulate collisions with a stack of surviving asteroids.
slides.narration: Simulate collisions with a stack of surviving asteroids.

slides.heading: Brute force vs optimal
bullets: Stack of survivors → each pushed/popped once, O(n)
slides.narration: Re-simulating until nothing changes is quadratic. A stack of survivors handles each asteroid in amortised constant time, since each is pushed and popped at most once. Only a right-mover followed by a left-mover collides.

slides.heading: Approach
bullets: 2. A left mover destroys smaller right movers on top
slides.narration: Step by step. First, right movers push. Second, a left mover destroys smaller right movers on top. Third, equal sizes destroy both. Fourth, survivors remain.

slides.heading: Java solution
slides.narration: For each asteroid we loop while it's alive, moving left, and the top moves right. A smaller top is popped; otherwise equal sizes pop the top and either way the current one dies. Survivors are pushed.

slides.heading: Complexity
slides.narration: Time is O of n. Space is O of n.

slides.heading: Edge cases & pitfalls
slides.narration: A left-mover before a right-mover never collides. Equal sizes destroy both.
